Definition: to gush; by implication, to inundate, cleanse; by analogy, to gallop, conquer
KeyPassages: 1 Kings 22:38; Ezekiel 16:9; Isaiah 43:2; Song of Solomon 8:7
BiblicalUsage: To overflow is to wash, to rinse, to flood, and to drown. One washed Ahab's chariot in the pool of Samaria, and the dogs licked up his blood; God washed Jerusalem with water and anointed her with oil; and Isaiah promises that when thou passest through the waters, they shall not overflow thee. The Song says many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the waters in this word are both judgment and mercy. They wash the chariot and drown the flood, they cleanse Jerusalem and cannot quench love, and I hold that the God who sends the flood is the God who carries His people through it.
RelatedBooks: 1 Kings; Ezekiel; Isaiah; Song of Solomon
